docs.text: Standard operating procedures: how the recurring things get done, written down once so nobody has to hold it in their head.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
The site is live and the content tree is empty. This page is the whole of it.

Procedures land here one at a time, as they get written. Not as a bulk import of filed paperwork nobody has read since it was filed -- a page that arrives without being re-read arrives already wrong, and this site has exactly one reader who would be the person to discover that.

docs.title: What belongs here
docs.text:
Procedures, checklists, standards, and the paperwork trail described in the abstract. How a thing is done, in a form somebody could follow without asking.

Not anything naming a person or a number: borrower names, balances, payoff figures, account numbers, addresses tied to somebody. That lives in FileMaker and it stays there.

This site is public, and no setting changes that

A GitHub Pages site is reachable by anyone even when its repository is private. An unlisted URL is obscurity, not access control, and a crawler does not need to be told where to look. The test before writing anything here is one question: if a stranger read this page, would it matter? If yes, it does not go on this site.

docs.title: Writing for this site
docs.text:
The authoring contract is shared across every site in this family and is documented once, on the template site, which is a live example of every rule it states:

  • The frontmatter contract
  • Writing a page: callouts, tabs, tables
  • Links between pages and between sites

Those are cross-site links. They resolve through the peer's published page index at build time rather than by anybody hardcoding a URL, which is why they survive the other site reorganising itself.
